about:
# Next

Quest-targeting addon for **WoW Classic Era 1.15.9 (Interface 11509)**, **Burning Crusade Classic 2.5.6 (20506)**, **Mists of Pandaria Classic 5.5.4 (50504)**, **WoW Forever 1.60.1 (16001)**, and **Retail 12.1.5 (120105)**.

- **Next quest target.**
- **Next RestedXP guide target.**
- **Next mob to farm with ItemTree.**
- **Next rare in range with RareScanner.**

**Your next target, one button away.**

**[Download the latest release](https://github.com/simonrath/next/releases/latest)**

The master button can also target the current guide step from Follow The Arrow.
Enable **Follow The Arrow guide targets** under **Buttons & Bar** and keep the
**FTA Target** macro enabled in Follow The Arrow. The current Retail edition
of Follow The Arrow does not provide that macro.

## Installation

Starting with 1.8.1, download `Next-<version>.zip` for any supported client: Retail, Classic,
TBC, Mists, or Forever. The same ZIP works on all five and contains only `QuestTargets/`. Close WoW and replace
`Interface/AddOns/QuestTargets` with the folder from the ZIP.

For Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic, Mists of Pandaria Classic, and Forever,
install and enable **QuestieDB** separately from
[CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/questiedb) or the
[official QuestieDB releases](https://github.com/Questie/QuestieDB/releases/).
Choose the version for your client. QuestieDB is no longer included in Next.
If QuestieDB is already installed, keep it and update it separately.
QuestieDB supplies data only; keep the full Questie addon enabled to use its tracker.

Retail needs no QuestieDB and reads objectives from the Retail quest log. Mob names
come from readable quest text and visible nameplates. Item sources and turn-in NPCs
without names in the quest text are not inferred on Retail.

## Features

The [patch notes](https://github.com/simonrath/next/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) follow the selected addon's language and open
once on the first login with a new version. Open them again under
**Options → AddOns → Next → Patch Notes**.

Release maintainers: [Set up automatic CurseForge publishing](https://github.com/simonrath/next/blob/main/docs/curseforge-publishing.md).

Next also appears under **Options → Keybindings → Next**.
The master, focused quest, ItemTree and RareScanner actions support two binding slots each.
Native changes, including clearing a focused-quest binding, are kept across
refreshes and reloads. In the addon's own Hotkeys section, assigning an occupied
keyboard/controller key requires confirmation before replacing its old action.

- One target button per quest and a master button for active objectives.
- The master button combines quest mobs, ready turn-ins and targets from enabled modules. Targets with nearer known coordinates come first.
- Name targeting and nearby nameplate detection.
- Configurable target markers, hotkeys, and tooltips.
- Compact native addon settings in every supported client, with a minimap button and a resizable, movable compass button bar.
- Quest-specific target buttons appear automatically beside quest rows in Questie's tracker when Questie is installed and enabled.
- Right-click a quest icon in either quest list to focus that quest. The always-visible focus highlight is shared between both lists; a separate configurable hotkey targets only the focused quest while the master button keeps its normal behavior.
- **RestedXP:** Enable **Show RestedXP button** under **Buttons & Bar > Targeting Bar: Modules**. The blue compass looks for targets in your active guide step, including mobs, quest NPCs and flight masters. The master button includes these guide targets alongside targets from its other sources.
- **RareScanner on WoW Forever:** Click a rare icon on the world map to mark it, then use the purple compass or its hotkeys to search marked rares. Enable **Scan all rares in zone** under **Buttons & Bar > Targeting Bar: Modules** to include unmarked rares and known dungeon rares. Click a rare icon on the minimap to look for that rare directly.
- **Polestar on WoW Forever:** Enable **Follow Polestar guide targets** under **Buttons & Bar > Targeting Bar: Modules** to use the main compass for named, open goals in the displayed Polestar step. You can enable both guide integrations at the same time. Secure updates wait until combat ends.
- Optional transparency mode immediately leaves only the quest list visible. Its toggle icon hides two seconds after the cursor leaves the window and reappears when the cursor moves anywhere over it. A 90% transparent draggable strip is shown only while the cursor is over the window.
- The compact quest window has adjacent Settings and Feedback buttons; quest data also refreshes automatically or with `/qt refresh`.
- Under **Buttons & Bar**, choose the visible compasses in **Targeting Bar: Modules**. Adjust orientation, scale, spacing, the bronze border and dividers in **Targeting Bar: Appearance & Position**.
- English, German, Spanish, French, Turkish, and Simplified Chinese.
- In-game feedback button with a copyable link and a QR code for
  [the public feedback form](https://feedback.jacknine.org/). Scan the code with
  your phone to submit feedback; no GitHub account is needed.

Use `/qt` to open the quest window and `/qt settings` to open settings.
Under **Hotkeys**, each action has two binding buttons side by side,
like WoW's native keybinding rows. Click either slot and press a keyboard key or
an Xbox/controller button, middle/extra mouse button, or scroll the mouse wheel.
Ctrl, Alt, and Shift modifiers also work with mouse inputs. While listening,
left- or right-click cancels assignment; these primary mouse buttons are reserved.
Keep the pointer over the binding button when assigning mouse input.
Changing or clearing one slot keeps the other binding;
when the first slot is cleared, the remaining binding moves into it. The controller must already be recognized by WoW
and native gamepad input must be enabled (`/console GamePadEnable 1` on clients
that support it). Escape cancels assignment; Delete or Backspace clears the selected slot.
Clients without the gamepad frame API retain keyboard binding support.
To position the bar, open **Buttons & Bar > Targeting Bar: Appearance & Position > Move bar**.
Outside combat, drag the handle with the left mouse button; the native move cursor
shows where you can drag. Choose **Done** to save, **Cancel** or Escape to restore
the previous position, or **Reset position** to preview the default position.
Holding the right mouse button and dragging the master button still works directly.
If combat starts during editing, editing ends and the last released position is
saved after combat. The positioning controls are available even with tooltips off.
Targeting is subject to the client's protected-action and combat restrictions.
Under **Target markers**, **Mute dead-target clearing sound** optionally suppresses
the deselection sound for 100 ms when a Next button or hotkey replaces
a dead NPC. It is off by default and adds no macro bytes. Selection sounds and
living-target changes stay audible; another playback of the same deselection
sound during the short window is also muted. Standalone action-bar macros are
not covered. In-game timing still needs validation on each supported client.
See [the detailed documentation](https://github.com/simonrath/next/blob/main/QuestTargets/README.md) for behavior and limitations.

## Development

Follow the [internal patch notes guide](https://github.com/simonrath/next/blob/main/docs/patch-notes-guide.md) for every
change. Maintain the German player history in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/simonrath/next/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
and its five translations under [docs/changelog](https://github.com/simonrath/next/blob/main/docs/changelog). Run
`./tools/update_patch_notes.ps1` before packaging. The English in-game history
is separate from the English CurseForge notes for a specific release.

The patch notes use the scrollable version-card pattern from
[FlareUI's What's New panel](https://github.com/malkkav/FlareUI/blob/main/Settings/Panel.lua).
The Next entry in Options uses the existing action-row pattern
from `QuestTargetsMoveSettingMixin` in `QuestTargets/UI.lua`.
The window uses Blizzard templates, following the existing
`DefaultPanelFlatTemplate` and NineSlice setup in `UI.Create`.

Install Python dependencies with `python -m pip install -r tests/requirements.txt`.
Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_quest_targets*.py"`.
Database integration tests use the pinned QuestieDB v1.0.9 Vanilla archive in
the system temporary directory at
`quest-targets-questiedb-v1.0.9/QuestieDB-Vanilla.zip`. Package tests verify that every flavor contains Next only;
building packages requires no QuestieDB download or provider cache.

Build the universal release package with PowerShell:

```powershell
./tools/package_quest_targets.ps1
```

The result is `dist/Next-<version>.zip`, shared by all five clients.
It contains runtime Lua, XML, TOC, and texture files only. Tests, documentation,
and QuestieDB are excluded. Legacy `-Flavor`, `-AddonOnly`, and `-CurseForge`
arguments remain accepted and produce the same universal archive.

Build a test package with a unique version and filename:

```powershell
./tools/package_quest_targets.ps1 -PreviewVersion 1.6.1
```

The ZIP name and its embedded TOC version include a UTC timestamp, such as
`Next-1.8.1-preview.20261124-120000-123Z.zip`. This makes installed test
builds distinguishable in the options heading. The source TOC is preserved.
Existing archives are never overwritten. Use `-OutputDirectory <folder>` for
another destination. Package tests build in temporary directories so they
cannot replace downloaded release files.

## License

[GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE](https://github.com/simonrath/next/blob/main/LICENSE) for Next only.

### QuestieDB attribution

Next accesses the separately installed QuestieDB addon through its public
API. QuestieDB code and data belong to the [QuestieDB team and its contributors](https://github.com/Questie/QuestieDB).
QuestieDB has been a separate download since version 1.4.2. See the
[QuestieDB notice](https://github.com/simonrath/next/blob/main/QuestTargets/QUESTIEDB-NOTICE.md) for earlier package provenance.

releases.name: Next 1.8.3
releases.notes:
# Next 1.8.3

### FlareUI
- **New: FlareUI support!** Enable **FlareUI integration** under **Buttons & Bar** to show a Next targeting button beside supported quests in FlareUI’s tracker. Left-click to target and right-click to focus the quest. Requires FlareUI 7.0.17 or later on Forever. Buttons hide in combat.

### Quest list
- **Quest buttons:** Clicking again keeps a living target for that quest selected. This applies to the Next quest list and the buttons in Questie, EllesmereUI and FlareUI.

### ItemTree
- The **ItemTree button** tooltip lists all currently imported mobs.

### Targeting bar
- **Targeting bar** tooltip titles now start with **Next**. The master button makes it clearer what it searches and how to move the bar.

Next supports Forever, Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic Anniversary, Mists of Pandaria Classic and Retail. The FlareUI integration requires Forever.

releases.name: Next 1.8.2
releases.notes:
# Next 1.8.2

### Follow The Arrow
- **New: Follow The Arrow support!** Under **Buttons & Bar**, enable **Follow The Arrow guide targets**. The master button uses the current guide step’s targets from **FTA Target**, including without QuestieDB. Enable the macro in Follow The Arrow. The current Retail version of Follow The Arrow does not provide it.

Thanks to **EscapeKeyEscapee** for suggesting Follow The Arrow support!

### Polestar
- The **Master Button** tries the current Polestar target first when QuestieDB is absent and RestedXP provides no targets.
- If Polestar is your only guide addon, the missing QuestieDB popup no longer appears at login.
- The **Master Button** now includes creatures Polestar lists for collecting items or using a quest item.
- When you use Polestar without QuestieDB, the quest window shows how to enable Polestar targeting in Next.

### RareScanner
- The **RareScanner button** now respects **Show button tooltips**.
- With a single rare in the list, the purple button clears dead targets with every marking setting.
- **Zone search** loads spawn locations in small batches. Target names are available immediately.

### Performance
- Nameplate changes no longer reload the entire quest log. The targeting bar and tracker buttons do less work when targets and settings stay the same.

# Next 1.8.1

- **Next** is the addon's name starting with version 1.8.1. Your settings and keybinds carry over when you update.

releases.name: Quest Targets 1.8.0
releases.notes:
# Quest Targets 1.8.0

## Massive Improvements

- **One Master Button for your active targets.** The master button searches the quest log and your enabled RestedXP, Polestar, ItemTree and RareScanner sources together. Outside combat, each click puts nearby targets with known coordinates first, including NPCs ready for quest turn-ins.
- **Search all modules** is on by default under **Show master button**. Turn it off to search only quest log targets with the master button. The blue button searches RestedXP guide targets.
- **RareScanner** checks nearby readable nameplates first and updates the distance order on every click outside combat, including while standing still.

## Target markers

- Under **Target Markers**, choose **Raid marker**, **Ping**, or **No marking** for each targeting button. **Ping** is available in WoW Forever and Retail. WoW’s own settings control whether pings show in chat.

Thanks to **Caedis** for suggesting target pings!

## Options

- Addon settings are organized under **Quest Targets** and **Buttons & Bar**. Open **Patch Notes** and **Feedback** under **General**.
- Under **Appearance & Position**, enable **Show bar background** for a dark WoW background behind the button bar. The bronze border is slightly thicker and the dividers stay centered.

## Known Issues

- In the German WoW Forever client, some NPC names vary by gender. QuestieDB supplies one form per NPC, so exact-name searches can miss the variant shown in-game, such as **Diebin der Wüstenläufer**.

**Supported clients:** WoW Forever, Retail, Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic and Mists of Pandaria Classic.

releases.name: Quest Targets 1.7.5
releases.notes:
# Quest Targets 1.7.5

## Polestar on WoW Forever

- With Polestar installed, turn on **Follow Polestar guide targets** under **Buttons > Targeting bar**. Your master button searches NPCs from the displayed guide step, including alternate sources for collection goals. A valid friendly NPC stays selected when you click again.
- If the guide step has no target, the master button falls back to your quest objectives. If both guide integrations are active and available, RestedXP takes priority.

Thanks to **postblink** for the Polestar integration!
